edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: I. Apprehensi sunt adolescentes catechumini, Revocatus et Felicitas conserva ejus, Saturninus et Secundulus. Inter quos et Vivia Perpetua, honeste nata, liberaliter instituta, matronaliter nupta, habens patrem et matrem et fratres duos, alterum aeque catechuminum, et filium infantem ad ubera. Erat autem ipsa annorum circiter viginti duorum. Haec ordinem totum martyrii sui jam hinc ipsa narrabit, sicut conscriptum manu sua et suo sensu reliquit. II. « Cum adhuc, inquit, cum persecutoribus essemus, et me pater avertere et dejicere pro sua affectione perseveraret: Pater, inquio, vides, verbi gratia, vas hoc jacens, urceolum, sive aliud? » Et « dixit: Video. » Et ego dixi ei: « Numquid alio nomine vocari potest quam quod est? » Et ait: « Non. » « Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum, nisi quod sum Christiana. » Tunc pater motus in hoc verbo, misit « se in me ut oculos mihi erueret: sed vexavit tantum, et profectus est victus cum argumentis diaboli, Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patre, Domino gratias egi, et refrigeravit absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; mihi autem Spiritus dictavit nihil aliud petendum in aqua, nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem, et expavi, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! aestus validos turbarum beneficio concussurae militum: novissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis. Ibi tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diacones, qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut, paucis horis emissi, in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere universi sibi vacabant. Ego infantem lactabam jam inedia defectum. Sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem, et confortabam fratrem, commendabam filium. Tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere videram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpavi ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim convalui, et relevata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis: et factus est mihi carcer subito quasi praetorium, ut ibi mallem esse quam alibi. « III. Tunc dixit mihi frater meus: Domina soror, jam in magna dignitate es; et tanta ut postules visionem, et ostendatur tibi an passio sit, an commeatus. Et ego, quae me sciebam fabulari cum Domino, cujus beneficia tanta experta eram, fidenter repromisi ei dicens: « Crastina die tibi renuntiabo. » Et postulavi, et ostensum est mihi hoc: Video scalam auream mirae magnitudinis pertingentem usque ad coelum et angustam, per quam non nisi singuli ascendere possent: et in lateribus scalae omne genus ferramentorum infixum. Erant ibi gladii, lanceae, hami, machaerae; ut si quis negligenter, aut non sursum adtendens ascenderet, laniaretur et carnes ejus inhaererent ferramentis. Et erat sub ipsa scala draco cubans mirae magnitudinis, qui ascendentibus insidias parabat, et exterrebat ne ascenderent. Ascendit autem Saturus prior, qui postea se propter nos ultro tradiderat, et tunc cum adducti sumus, praesens non fuerat: et pervenit in caput scalae, et convertit se ad me, et dixit mihi: « Perpetua, sustineo te. Sed vide ne te mordeat draco ille. » Et dixi ego: « Non me nocebit in nomine Domini Jesu Christi. » Et de sub ipsa scala quasi timens me, lente elevavit caput: et cum primum gradum calcassem, calcavi illius caput. Et ascendi et vidi spatium horti immensum, et in medio horti sedentem hominem canum, in habitu pastoris, grandem, oves mulgentem; et circumstantes candidati millia multa. Et levavit caput et adspexit me, et dixit mihi: « Bene venisti, tecnon. » Et clamavit me, et de caseo quod mulgebat dedit mihi quasi buccellam, et ego accepi junctis manibus, et manducavi: et universi circumstantes dixerunt, Amen. Et ad sonum vocis experrecta sum, commanducans adhuc dulcis nescio quid. Et retuli statim fratri meo, et intelleximus passionem esse futuram: et coepimus nullam jam spem in saeculo habere.
pass_a_gloss: Adolescents, catechumens, were seized, Revocatus and Felicity, his fellow servant, Saturninus and Secundulus, among whom also Vivia Perpetua, born honorably, educated liberally, married matronally, having a father and a mother and two brothers, one of whom was also a catechumen, and an infant son at her breast, she was about twenty-two years old, she will now narrate the whole order of her martyrdom, as she left it written in her own hand and her own sense, while we were still with the persecutors, and my father was trying to turn me away and cast me down because of his affection, Father, I say, you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a little jug, or something else, and he said, I see, and I said to him, can it be called by any other name than what it is, and he said, no, thus I also cannot say that I am anything other than what I am, a Christian, then my father, moved by this word, threw himself at me to gouge out my eyes, but he only harassed me and went away defeated, overcome by the devil's arguments, then, after a few days, when I had been without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and his absence was a relief to me, in that same space of a few days, we were baptized, and the Spirit dictated to me that I should ask for nothing else in the water except the endurance of the flesh, after a few days, we were taken back to prison, and I was terrified because I had never experienced such darkness, oh, bitter day, strong heat of the crowds, thanks to the disturbance of the soldiers, finally, I was worn out by worry about my infant, there, Tertius and Pomponius, blessed deacons, who were ministering to us, arranged for a reward, so that, released for a few hours, we might refresh ourselves in a better part of the prison, then, going out of the prison, everyone was taking care of themselves, I was nursing my infant, who was already failing from hunger, I was worried about him, I spoke to my mother, and I comforted my brother, I commended my son, I was wasting away because I saw them wasting away because of me, I suffered such worries for many days, and I managed to have my infant stay with me in prison, and immediately I recovered, and I was relieved of the labor and worry of my infant, and the prison suddenly became like a palace to me, so that I preferred to be there rather than anywhere else, then my brother said to me, Lady sister, you are now in great dignity, and so great that you can ask for a vision, and it will be shown to you whether it is passion or reprieve, and I, who knew that I was speaking with the Lord, whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, tomorrow I will tell you, and I asked, and it was shown to me, I see a golden ladder of great size reaching up to heaven, narrow, so that only one person could ascend at a time, and on the sides of the ladder, every kind of iron tool was fixed, there were swords, lances, hooks, and knives, so that if someone were to ascend carelessly, or not paying attention upwards, they would be torn and their flesh would stick to the iron tools, and under the ladder, a dragon of great size was lying, preparing ambushes for those ascending, and frightening them so that they would not ascend, however, Saturus ascended first, who later had handed himself over voluntarily on our behalf, and when we were led away, he was not present, and he reached the top of the ladder, and turned to me, and said to me, Perpetua, I am waiting for you, but see that the dragon does not bite you, and I said, it will not harm me in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and from under the ladder, as if fearing me, it slowly lifted its head, and when I had stepped on the first rung, I stepped on its head, and I ascended, and I saw a space of a garden, immense, and in the middle of the garden, a man, canum, in the dress of a shepherd, large, milking sheep, and thousands of white-robed candidates standing around, and he lifted his head, and looked at me, and said to me, you have come well, child, and he called me, and gave me a little piece of the cheese he was milking, and I received it with joined hands, and I ate, and all those standing around said, Amen, and at the sound of the voice, I woke up, still chewing something sweet, and I immediately told my brother, and we understood that it would be a passion, and we began to have no hope in the world

lemmas.gloss: grey-haired or white-haired, but here describing a man with a sheep-like quality

choices.why: the Latin text uses 'canum' to describe the man, which could imply a sheep-like quality
the Latin text uses 'urceolum' as an example of a vessel
the Latin text lists 'machaerae' as one of the iron tools on the ladder
the Latin text uses 'buccellam' to describe the piece of cheese given to Perpetua
the Latin text uses 'tecnnon' as a term of endearment

pass_b_english: While we were still among the persecutors, my father kept trying to turn me away and cast me down because of his affection for me. "Father," I said, "do you see, for example, this vessel lying here — a little jug, or something else?" He answered, "I see." And I said to him, "Can it be called by any other name than what it is?" He replied, "No." "So too I cannot call myself anything other than what I am, a Christian." Then my father, moved by this word, threw himself at me to gouge out my eyes. But he only harassed me and went away defeated, overcome by the devil's arguments. After a few days, when I had been without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and his absence was a relief to me.

In that same short time we were baptized, and the Spirit dictated to me that I should ask for nothing in the water except the endurance of the flesh. After a few days we were taken back to prison, and I was terrified because I had never experienced such darkness. Oh, bitter day: the intense heat, the crush of the crowds, and the rough handling by the soldiers. Finally I was worn out by worry for my infant. There Tertius and Pomponius, blessed deacons who ministered to us, arranged by a bribe that we should be let out for a few hours to refresh ourselves in a better part of the prison. When we went out of the prison, everyone attended to their own needs. I was nursing my infant, who was already failing from hunger. Anxious for him, I spoke to my mother and comforted my brother, commending my son to them. I was wasting away because I saw them wasting away on my account. I endured such anxieties for many days, and I obtained permission for my infant to stay with me in prison. Immediately I recovered, and was relieved of the labor and worry over the child. The prison suddenly became like a palace to me, so that I would rather be there than anywhere else.

Then my brother said to me, "Lady sister, you are now in great dignity, so great that you can ask for a vision, and it will be shown to you whether it is martyrdom or release." And I, who knew that I spoke with the Lord, whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, "Tomorrow I will tell you." I asked, and this was shown to me: I see a golden ladder of marvelous size reaching up to heaven, and narrow, so that only one person can ascend at a time. On the sides of the ladder every kind of iron tool is fixed — swords, lances, hooks, and knives — so that if anyone ascends carelessly, or without looking upward, he will be torn and his flesh will cling to the iron tools. And beneath the ladder a dragon of marvelous size lies crouching, preparing ambushes for those who ascend and frightening them so that they will not ascend. But Saturus ascended first; he later handed himself over voluntarily on our behalf, and when we were led away he was not present. He reached the top of the ladder, turned to me, and said, "Perpetua, I am waiting for you. But see that the dragon does not bite you." And I said, "It will not harm me in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ." And from beneath the ladder, as if fearing me, it slowly lifted its head. When I stepped on the first rung, I stepped on its head. I ascended and saw an immense garden, and in the middle of the garden a white-haired man sitting, dressed as a shepherd, tall, milking sheep. Thousands of white-robed people stood around him. He lifted his head, looked at me, and said to me, "Welcome, child." He called me over and gave me a morsel of the cheese he was milking. I received it with joined hands and ate, and all those standing around said, "Amen." At the sound of the voice I woke up, still chewing something sweet. I immediately told my brother, and we understood that it would be martyrdom. And we began to have no hope left in this world.

review.notes: Pass B fails to translate 'hominem canum' accurately according to the provided lemmas and choices. The Latin 'hominem canum' is translated in Pass B as 'a white-haired man', whereas the Lemma/Choice section explicitly rejects 'white-haired man' in favor of 'a man, canum' to preserve the ambiguity/sheep-like quality of the Latin. Additionally, Pass B translates 'commeatus' as 'release', while Pass A translates it as 'reprieve'; while both are acceptable, the discrepancy in the handling of the 'canum' descriptor is a direct contradiction of the provided translation instructions/choices.
